findings.summary: assembleGenerateDeps evaluates resolveAgentRunBin() eagerly while constructing the spawnRuntime object literal, so the whole dep assembly throws AgentRunUnresolvedError whenever 'agent-run' is not on PATH and AGENT_RUN_BIN is unset — even though spawnRuntime.agentRunBin is only needed if a generation role is actually spawned. Four acceptance sites reach this line with no AGENT_RUN_BIN stub: the U5 positive test (test/g4c-generate-wiring.test.ts:597), the U7 T5 discriminative test (:705), and the U1 T1 discriminative test (:250, via runChannelWrite with no injected generateDeps). Every other test in the repo that touches this code path stubs AGENT_RUN_BIN first (test/tick-run.test.ts:852-853, :1206-1207, :1230-1231; test/a8f-adddir.test.ts:154-155, :292-293), which shows the harness does not otherwise guarantee a resolvable agent-run. The three decisive discriminative assertions for U1/U5/U7 are therefore host-environment-dependent: on a clean machine they fail with AgentRunUnresolvedError rather than exercising what they claim to check. This is precisely the '评审判过 ≠ 命令跑过' failure mode that spec §0 names as the single most important rule of the package and that caused the previous development to FAIL dd acceptance. resolveAgentRunBin must be deferred into spawnProcess (lazy) so dep assembly cannot fail on an unrelated binary lookup.

U5's negative case still has zero discriminating power against production code, repeating verbatim the major finding already raised against attempt 2 (.dev-dispatch/reviews/rf-attempt_01KZKHZHW2H7PA7BMZ3TPSBBBD/review.json). Spec U5 requires 'EXPORT_ROOT 未配置 ⇒ 响亮失败' proven by 正反两例. The test hand-writes its own spawnExport stub that re-implements the production guard ('const exportRoot = process.env.EXPORT_ROOT; if (!exportRoot) throw new MissingExportRootError();') and injects it via generateDeps, so it asserts only that its own stub throws. Deleting or inverting the real guard at src/tick-run.ts:1326-1327 would leave this test green. The attempt added a positive case driving assembleGenerateDeps but left the negative case still mirroring rather than driving production, so the mutation 'remove the production EXPORT_ROOT check' survives.

U10's evidence is internally inconsistent and, given the eager resolveAgentRunBin defect above, cannot be relied upon. The dev-note's conclusion (line 17) and the pasted tail (lines 47-48) state '22 files / 411 tests', while the immediately preceding final review of this same development recorded the attempt-2 dev-note claiming 409 tests for a test file described identically as 20 cases; the note gives no account of what changed the total. Spec U10 additionally demands the run be performed with DOC_CHANNEL and RESEARCH_ORIGIN unset; the note asserts this in prose (line 53) but the pasted block carries no evidence of the environment. As a read-only reviewer I cannot execute the command, and the acceptance criterion the spec calls decisive therefore remains unverified.

The U1 T1 discriminative test relies on vi.spyOn against an ESM namespace object obtained via dynamic import, while the production call site in runChannelWrite calls runGenerate through a static named import binding (src/tick-run.ts:49, called at :1567). This pattern's effectiveness depends entirely on Vitest's Vite transform rewriting exports into reconfigurable getters; the repo pins no vitest.config file and this is the only spyOn-on-module usage in the entire test suite, so there is no established precedent in-repo confirming the pattern works here. If the spy does not intercept the static binding, the assertion expect(generateSpy).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1) would fail rather than silently pass, but combined with the blocker above the T1 mutation coverage claimed in the dev-note's mutation matrix is not demonstrably established.
